### Volumito Configuration Files

The `volumito configuration` command group lets you manage
the `volumito` configuration files:

```bash
volumito configuration --help
Usage: volumito configuration [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Create, check, and search for volumito configuration files.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  check   Check that a configuration file is correct and print the values...
  create  Create a configuration file with all known keys set to their...
  search  List every probed configuration path, marking those found and...
```

#### The Configuration File

A Volumito configuration file is a
[YAML](https://yaml.org/)
file that looks like this:

```yaml
# volumito CLI configuration file
#
# Generated with default values for version 0.0.52: edit as needed (and remove this comment)

aliases:
  # Aliases/shorthands for existing command paths (groups, commands, subcommands).
  # Limitations:
  # - An alias must resolve to an existing (sub)command, otherwise an error is produced
  # - An alias cannot shadow a built-in command
  # - Options are not supported in the definition of the alias (only command paths)
  # - Aliases are not listed by --help: list them with "volumito command alias"
  # c: collection
  # cb: collection browse
  # cmd: command
  # cmda: command alias
  # cmdl: command list
  # conf: configuration
  # cs: collection search
  # exec: system execute
  # i: info
  # mlt: multiroom
  # mltz: multiroom zones
  # mute: playback mute
  # next: playback next
  # not: notification
  # notl: notification list
  # notlis: notification listen
  # notr: notification register
  # notu: notification unregister
  # p: playback
  # pause: playback pause
  # ping: system ping
  # pl: playlist
  # play: playback play
  # pld: playlist download
  # pll: playlist list
  # plp: playlist play
  # pm: playback mute
  # pnext: playback next
  # ppause: playback pause
  # pplay: playback play
  # pprev: playback previous
  # prev: playback previous
  # ps: playback status
  # pseek: playback seek
  # pstop: playback stop
  # pt: playback toggle
  # pu: playback unmute
  # pv: playback volume
  # q: queue
  # qc: queue clear
  # qd: queue download
  # ql: queue list
  # qr: queue replace
  # qs: queue status
  # s: story
  # salb: story album
  # sart: story artist
  # scre: story credits
  # seek: playback seek
  # slab: story label
  # spla: story place
  # stop: playback stop
  # sys: system
  # syse: system execute
  # sysi: system info
  # sysp: system ping
  # sysv: system version
  # t: track
  # ta: track audio
  # tc: track albumart
  # ti: track info
  # toggle: playback toggle
  # unmute: playback unmute
  # vol: playback volume


downloads:
  # A key here applies to all relevant commands;
  # overrides can be specified under the following sections:
  # - playlist-download
  # - queue-download
  # - track-albumart
  # - track-audio

  # Write a JSON manifest next to the downloaded file (e.g., out.flac.json)
  create-download-manifest: true

  # Directory to download into, created if missing (mutually exclusive with output-file);
  # "{timestamp}" in the path is replaced with the current UTC time (e.g., 20260726121314)
  # output-directory: .                           # use the current working directory
  # output-directory: /tmp/volumito               # use a fixed directory
  # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/{timestamp}   # use a per-run timestamped directory
  output-directory: null                          # no download by default

  # Exact file path to download to (mutually exclusive with output-directory)
  # output-file: /tmp/volumito.out      # use a fixed full path
  output-file: null                     # no download by default

  # Overwrite the destination file if it already exists
  overwrite-existing-files: false

  # Characters to replace in the file name generated from the template
  replace-characters-in-file-names: " :"

  # Replacement string for the replaced characters
  replace-characters-in-file-names-with: "_"

  playlist-download:
    # Template (Python str.format) for the album art file names
    albumart-file-name-template: '000___{album}___{artist}.{extension}'

    # Template (Python str.format) for the audio file names
    audio-file-name-template: '{position:03d}___{title}___{album}___{artist}.{extension}'

    # Path of the download manifest
    manifest-file: '{output_directory}/manifest.json'

    # Number of retries waiting for the next track's metadata to become current
    number-retries-next-track: 10

    # Download only the tracks at these queue positions (e.g., '1-3,6-8,12')
    only-tracks: null

    # Download each album's cover (once per cover)
    with-albumart: true

    # Add your own overrides here
    # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/playlist              # use a fixed directory
    # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/playlist/{timestamp}  # use a per-run directory

  queue-download:
    # Template (Python str.format) for the album art file names
    albumart-file-name-template: '{artist}/{album_volume}/000___{album}.{extension}'

    # Template (Python str.format) for the audio file names
    audio-file-name-template: '{artist}/{album_volume}/{tracknumber:03d}___{title}.{extension}'

    # Path of the download manifest
    manifest-file: '{output_directory}/manifest.json'

    # Number of retries waiting for the next track's metadata to become current
    number-retries-next-track: 10

    # Download only the tracks at these queue positions (e.g., '1-3,6-8,12')
    only-tracks: null

    # Download each album's cover (once per cover)
    with-albumart: true

    # Add your own overrides here
    # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/queue                 # use a fixed directory
    # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/queue/{timestamp}     # use a per-run directory

  track-albumart:
    # Template (Python str.format) for the -d output file name
    file-name-template: '000___{album}___{artist}.{extension}'

    # Add your own overrides here
    # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/covers                # use a fixed directory
    # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/covers/{timestamp}    # use a per-run directory

  track-audio:
    # Template (Python str.format) for the -d output file name
    file-name-template: '{position:03d}___{title}___{album}___{artist}.{extension}'

    # Add your own overrides here
    # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/audio                 # use a fixed directory
    # output-directory: /tmp/volumito/audio/{timestamp}     # use a per-run directory


miscellaneous:
  # Embed track metadata and cover art into the downloaded audio file
  add-cover-and-metadata: true

  # When copying local files (from /mnt),
  # allow renaming them after the file name template
  allow-local-file-rename: false

  # Check that each queue-download track's metadata are current before downloading it
  check-next-track: true

  # Check that the playlist name exists before playing it
  check-playlist-name: true

  # Check that the seek position is within the duration of the current track
  check-seek-position: true

  # After running the "system execute" command,
  # return the same exit code generated on the Volumio host
  propagate-remote-exit-code: true


notification:
  # A key here applies to the listen, register, and unregister commands;
  # the keys of the options only "listen" has are under its own section

  # Path served by the local notification listener
  endpoint: /volumionotifications

  # Port the local notification listener binds to
  port: 3003

  listen:
    # Stop after receiving this number of notifications
    count: null

    # Stop after this number of seconds without receiving a notification
    idle-timeout: null

    # Register the URL if it is not registered yet
    register-url: false

    # URL to register, overriding the one composed from the port and the endpoint
    register-url-full: null

    # Stop after listening for this number of seconds
    timeout: null

    # On exit, unregister the URL registered by this run
    unregister-url-on-exit: true


output:
  # A key here applies to all relevant commands;
  # overrides can be specified under the following sections:
  # - collection-browse
  # - collection-search
  # - collection-statistics
  # - command-list
  # - multiroom-zones
  # - notification-list
  # - notification-listen
  # - playback-status
  # - playlist-list
  # - queue-list
  # - queue-status
  # - story-album
  # - story-artist
  # - story-credits
  # - story-label
  # - story-place
  # - system-execute
  # - system-info
  # - system-version
  # - track-info

  # Color the messages of the tool (when the terminal supports it)
  color: true

  # Fields to display.
  # Specify one of: ALL, SHORT, or a comma-separated list of fields (e.g., "album,artist")
  # - ALL: all fields returned by the host
  # - SHORT: a subset of most-useful fields, hardcoded in volumito
  # - comma-separated list of fields: only the specified fields
  fields: SHORT

  # Output format for all commands.
  # Available values are:
  # - json: JSON
  # - pretty: prettified JSON
  # - raw: as returned by the host
  # - table: tabular
  format: pretty

  # Produce machine-readable output only
  machine-readable: false

  # Print the data output through a pager (true) or directly (false)
  pager: false

  # Index queue positions starting at one (true) or zero (false)
  position-starting-at-one: true

  # After a playback or queue command like pause or clear, print the resulting playback status
  print-resulting-status: true

  # Turn non-fatal problems in this very file into errors, instead of ignoring them
  strict-parsing-configuration-file: false

  # Enable verbose output
  verbose: false

  collection-browse:
    # Browsing is meant for humans, so the table is its default format
    format: table

    # Add your own overrides here

  collection-search:
    # Searching is meant for humans, so the table is its default format
    format: table

    # Add your own overrides here

  collection-statistics:
    # Add your own overrides here

  command-list:
    # Print the aliases next to the command paths they point at
    # aliases: true

    # Print the command tree (true) or the flat command paths (false)
    # tree: true

    # Add your own overrides here

  multiroom-zones:
    # Add your own overrides here

  notification-list:
    # Add your own overrides here

  notification-listen:
    # Add your own overrides here

  playback-status:
    # Add your own overrides here

  playlist-list:
    # Add your own overrides here

  queue-list:
    # Add your own overrides here

  queue-status:
    # Add your own overrides here

  story-album:
    # Add your own overrides here

  story-artist:
    # Add your own overrides here

  story-credits:
    # Add your own overrides here

  story-label:
    # Add your own overrides here

  story-place:
    # Add your own overrides here

  system-execute:
    # Add your own overrides here

  system-info:
    # Add your own overrides here

  system-version:
    # Add your own overrides here

  track-info:
    # Add your own overrides here



timeouts:
  # MPD connection timeout, in seconds
  mpd-timeout: 5.0

  # Times to re-read the playback status until it reaches the expected state
  rest-api-retries-on-unexpected-state: 3

  # Seconds to sleep before the next REST API call
  rest-api-sleep-before-next-call: 2.0

  # REST API request timeout, in seconds
  rest-api-timeout: 5.0

  # REST API request timeout, in seconds, for slow endpoints
  # (e.g., replaceAndPlay, addToQueue)
  rest-api-timeout-slow-endpoints: 60.0


volumio:
  # Hostname or IP address of the Volumio host
  host: volumio.local

  # MPD port of the Volumio host
  # (defaults: 6600 for Volumio 4, 6599 for Volumio 3)
  mpd-port: 6600

  # REST API port of the Volumio host
  rest-api-port: 3000

  # URL scheme used to connect, one of http or https
  scheme: http

  # SSH password of the Volumio host, used to copy local files (from /mnt)
  #
  # IMPORTANT: setting this value (or using the --ssh-password option on the command line)
  #            leaves the password in clear text in this file or in the shell history;
  #            prefer using a private key that is authorized to SSH into the Volumio host
  #
  ssh-password: null

  # SSH port of the Volumio host, used to copy local files (from /mnt)
  ssh-port: 22

  # SSH user name on the Volumio host
  ssh-username: volumio
```

The keys in the file correspond to many of the options
offered by the CLI tool.
For example, the `volumio.host` key:

```yaml
...

volumio:
    host: volumio.local
...
```

correspond to the `--host` global option.

Similarly, the `notification.listen.count` key:

```yaml
...

notification:
    ...

    listen:
        # Stop after receiving this number of notifications
        count: null
```

corresponds to option `--count` of command `notification listen`.

A value of `null` means that the configuration file does not set that option,
thus not overriding the default value hardcoded in the CLI tool.

Any other value will override the hardcoded value,
if the configuration file is applied
(either located at one of the probed paths, or
explicitly specified with the `-c / --configuration-file` option).

#### Naming Convention

The `volumito` CLI tool automatically recognizes files named
`volumito.yaml` or `.volumito.yaml`.

You can call your configuration file with other names,
for instance `myvolumito.yaml`, but in that case you would need
to specify the `-c / --configuration-file` option each time you invoke `volumito`:

```bash
volumito -c /path/to/myvolumito.yaml ...
```

#### Probed Paths

By default, the following directories are probed, looking for
`volumito.yaml` or `.volumito.yaml` in them,
in the following order of decreasing priority:

- the current working directory;
- the user home directory (`~`);
- the `~/.volumito/` directory;
- the `~/.config/volumito/` directory;
- the `/etc/` directory (only on POSIX systems);
- the `/etc/volumito/` directory (only on POSIX systems).

The first configuration file found will be read and applied;
additional configuration files found will be ignored.

You can list all probed paths by running the `configuration search` command:

```bash
pwd
/home/alberto/projects/volumito/volumito/docs/cli
```

```bash
volumito configuration search
Configuration file locations, in probing order, in decreasing order of priority:
  /home/alberto/projects/volumito/volumito/docs/cli/volumito.yaml
  /home/alberto/projects/volumito/volumito/docs/cli/.volumito.yaml
  /home/alberto/volumito.yaml (found, used)
  /home/alberto/.volumito.yaml (found, NOT used)
  /home/alberto/.volumito/volumito.yaml
  /home/alberto/.volumito/.volumito.yaml
  /home/alberto/.config/volumito/volumito.yaml
  /home/alberto/.config/volumito/.volumito.yaml
  /etc/volumito.yaml
  /etc/.volumito.yaml
  /etc/volumito/volumito.yaml
  /etc/volumito/.volumito.yaml
```

#### Create A Configuration File

Given the naming and search convention described above,
it is advisable to store such a configuration file
in the user home directory, as `~/volumito.yaml` or `~/.volumito.yaml`,
so that it takes effect no matter the current directory
from which `volumito` is run from,
unless you prefer to have multiple per-directory configuration files
for some reason.

The `configuration create` command saves a good default template to file:

```bash
volumito configuration create -o ~/volumito.yaml
[2026-08-13T13:26:57.325Z] [INFO] Created configuration file "/home/alberto/volumito.yaml"
```

Without the `-o / --output-file` option, a `volumito.yaml` file
will be created in the current working directory.

Note that the command refuses to overwrite an existing file:

```bash
volumito configuration create -o ~/volumito.yaml
[2026-08-13T13:26:57.771Z] [ERRO] File already exists: "/home/alberto/volumito.yaml" (use --overwrite-existing-files to overwrite)
```

After creating your configuration file,
you might want to open it with your favorite text editor,
and modify it to suit your preferences.
In particular, you might want to check the connection parameters
under the `volumio` section.

If your Volumio host has a version < 4, add the
`--volumio-version 3` option so that the values
in the configuration file are created accordingly:

```bash
volumito configuration create -o ~/volumito3.yaml --volumio-version 3
[2026-08-13T13:26:58.218Z] [INFO] Created configuration file "/home/alberto/volumito3.yaml"
```

#### Ignore All Configuration Files

Sometimes it is useful to run `volumito` ignoring all configuration files
at the probed paths, thus ensuring to run the CLI tool with the hardcoded defaults
for all the commands and options.

To achieve that, the `-i / --ignore-configuration-file` global option is available:

```bash
volumito -i -H volumio3b.local playback status
{
    "album": "La Vie En Rouge",
    "artist": "Enrico Ruggeri",
    "bitdepth": "16 bit",
    "channels": 2,
    "duration": "00:04:08",
    "mute": false,
    "position": 3,
    "samplerate": "44 KHz",
    "seek": "00:03:49.563",
    "status": "play",
    "title": "La Vie En Rouge",
    "trackType": "qobuz",
    "volume": 20
}
```

The effect is clear with the `-v / --verbose` option specified:

```bash
volumito -v playback status
{
    "album": "La Vie En Rouge",
    "artist": "Enrico Ruggeri",
```

#### Priority

The value of an option is decided by, in order of descending priority:

- the explicit command line option  (e.g., `--host volumioexplicit.local`);
- the configuration file value (e.g., `volumio.host = anothervolumio.local`),
  if present, and unless the `-i / --ignore-configuration-file` option is issued;
- the value hardcoded in the implementation (e.g., `volumio.local`).

Examples, assuming the configuration file `~/volumito.yaml`
has `volumio.host = anothervolumio.local`:

```bash
# host will be "volumioexplicit.local" (explicit)
volumito --host volumioexplicit.local info

# host will be "anothervolumio.local" (configuration file)
volumito info

# host will be "volumio.local" (hardcoded, ignoring the configuration file)
volumito --ignore-configuration-file info
```
